mapping_definition.description: Declarative mapping of Sentinel DFIR detection findings to ATT&CK techniques. Each rule maps ONE technique (or sub-technique) to ONE tactic for findings of ONE detection rule, only when its conditions hold on the finding's recorded evidence. Edit this file to change mappings; the engine does not change.

confidence_scale.High: Every condition is met AND the mapping's own corroboration condition (documented per mapping) is also met AND the source finding's confidence is High.
confidence_scale.Medium: Every condition is met but the corroboration condition is not (or cannot be evaluated), or the source finding's confidence is Medium.
confidence_scale.Low: Every condition is met but the source finding's confidence is Low.

rules.tactic_reason: Guessing passwords is a way of obtaining credentials.

confidence.raise_reason: the failure count is at least twice the detection threshold

rules.rationale: {ctx.failure_count} failed logons for account '{ctx.grouping.target_account}' from {ctx.grouping.source_ip} within {ctx.window_seconds} s (threshold {ctx.threshold}); the recorded failure reasons ({ctx.failure_reasons}) are wrong-password failures, which is consistent with password guessing against one account.
rules.limitations: Repeated wrong-password failures also occur when a user or service retries stale credentials; the evidence does not show who or what produced them.

rules.tactic_reason: Brute force is a way of obtaining credentials.

confidence.raise_reason: the failure count is at least twice the detection threshold

rules.rationale: {ctx.failure_count} failed logons for account '{ctx.grouping.target_account}' from {ctx.grouping.source_ip} within {ctx.window_seconds} s (threshold {ctx.threshold}); the recorded failure reasons ({ctx.failure_reasons}) do not show password guessing specifically, so only the parent technique is mapped, consistent with brute force.
rules.limitations: Without wrong-password failure reasons the evidence cannot distinguish password guessing from other repeated-failure causes; no sub-technique is claimed.

rules.tactic_reason: PowerShell is used here to run commands and scripts.

confidence.raise_reason: both a process record and PowerShell script-block records show the execution

rules.rationale: PowerShell execution is recorded for PID {ctx.process.pid} on {finding.device} (user {finding.user}); the finding matched {indicators}. Consistent with PowerShell used for execution.
rules.limitations: The record shows PowerShell ran, not who intended it or why; administrators use PowerShell routinely.

rules.tactic_reason: Obfuscating a command impedes detection and analysis.

confidence.raise_reason: the decoded command text itself matched further indicators

rules.rationale: The PowerShell command line for PID {ctx.process.pid} carries a Base64 -EncodedCommand argument; ATT&CK lists Base64-encoded commands under command obfuscation. Consistent with an obfuscated command (finding matched {indicators}).
rules.limitations: Legitimate management tools also pass Base64-encoded commands; encoding alone does not show intent to evade.

rules.tactic_reason: Bringing a file in from an external system is part of the command-and-control phase.

confidence.raise_reason: a file record (files.json) shows a file was created at the path the script uses

rules.rationale: Script text for PID {ctx.process.pid} uses a download function and the finding's evidence includes a remote URL. Consistent with transferring a file from an external system into the host.
rules.limitations: A download function can also fetch ordinary content; without a created file the transfer of a tool is inferred, not shown.

rules.tactic_reason: A created account can be used to keep access to the system.

confidence.raise_reason: a process or script record shows the creation command naming the new account

rules.rationale: Event 4720 shows '{ctx.actor}' created account '{ctx.target_account}' on {finding.device}; the account's domain ({ctx.target_domain}) equals the device name, so it is a local account, and surrounding activity matched ({ctx.context_indicators_matched}). Consistent with creating a local account.
rules.limitations: Administrators create accounts routinely; the mapping rests on the surrounding suspicious activity the detection required, not on the creation alone.

rules.tactic_reason: A created account can be used to keep access to the system.

confidence.raise_reason: a process or script record shows the creation command naming the new account

rules.rationale: Event 4720 shows '{ctx.actor}' created account '{ctx.target_account}' on {finding.device}; surrounding activity matched ({ctx.context_indicators_matched}). The evidence does not show whether the account is local or domain, so only the parent technique is mapped.
rules.limitations: Without evidence that the account is local, no sub-technique is claimed.

rules.tactic_reason: Membership in a privileged local group raises the account's privileges (ATT&CK also lists Persistence for this technique).

confidence.raise_reason: the users.json snapshot independently lists the account as an administrator

rules.rationale: Event 4732 shows account '{ctx.target_account}' added to a privileged group after it was created by '{ctx.actor}', with surrounding activity ({ctx.context_indicators_matched}). Consistent with adding an account to additional local groups.
rules.limitations: Adding users to Administrators is also routine administration; the mapping rests on the surrounding suspicious activity the detection required.

not_mapped.reason: DET-001 groups failures per account; password spraying (one password against many accounts) would need failures across accounts from one source, which no implemented rule evaluates.
A successful logon shows the credentials were valid, not that an adversary used them. Valid Accounts spans four tactics and the evidence cannot choose one.
Same as T1078: a successful logon to a local account does not show adversary use, and the tactic cannot be chosen from the evidence.
Logon type 10 shows a Remote Desktop session, but lateral movement cannot be told apart from initial access; no rule establishes that the source was an internal system.
Needs evidence that the service is exposed and the source is external; under the default IP policy documentation-range sources are not external and no rule evaluates exposure.
wscript.exe appears only as the parent of PowerShell (unusual_parent) or as context in DET-003's process chain; no rule's conditions assert VBScript execution.
No rule establishes that a user opened a file.
A connection on a web port by PowerShell does not show command-and-control traffic.
Decoding is done by this project's analysis; the evidence does not record the adversary decoding anything.
